title: LLM4Vuln: A Unified Evaluation Framework for Decoupling and Enhancing LLMs' Vulnerability Reasoning

key_numbers.metric: knowledge-enhancement effect on F1 (Solidity, foundation models)
key_numbers.value: F1 nearly doubling on average with knowledge vs. without

key_numbers.metric: context-supplementation effect on TP counts across 36 knowledge x prompt combinations
key_numbers.value: Solidity 22/36 increased, Java 18/36 increased, C/C++ 28/36 increased

key_numbers.metric: zero-day validation
key_numbers.value: 14 confirmed vulnerabilities of 29 submitted, $3,576 in bounties across 4 projects

structure_gain: Context supplementation (caller/related-function context) increased TP in 22/36 (Solidity), 18/36 (Java), 28/36 (C/C++) knowledge x prompt combinations vs. the no-context condition, same model/budget (RQ2).
confound_note: Knowledge (Nk/Ok/Sk), context (with/without), and prompt scheme (raw/CoT) are each varied independently while holding the model and the other two dimensions fixed within each comparison cell -- a genuine 3-way representation/context ablation across 6 LLMs and 3 languages.
threats_to_datum: Context is supplied via static analysis 'for benchmarking purposes only' rather than real agentic retrieval; retrieved knowledge itself is imperfectly aligned with ground truth (only 36-68% of sampled retrieved knowledge matched ground truth), which could understate the true achievable benefit of context/knowledge.

title: Security Vulnerability Detection with Multitask Self-Instructed Fine-Tuning of Large Language Models

key_numbers.metric: F1 on BigVul (vs best baseline LineVul+DeepDFA)
F1 on PreciseBugs (post-cutoff, unseen) vs LineVul
GNN-embedding ablation on BigVul (MSIVD- vs MSIVD)

structure_gain: Adding CFG/DFA-derived GGNN embeddings to the fine-tuned LLM's hidden states raises F1 from 0.90 (LLM-only, MSIVD-) to 0.92 (MSIVD) on BigVul, holding the CodeLlama-13B backbone and training budget fixed (Table 4).
confound_note: The GNN-presence ablation (Table 4) cleanly holds model/budget fixed and varies only representation; but the headline BigVul-vs-baselines and BigVul-vs-PreciseBugs comparisons vary model, training data, and dataset simultaneously, and PreciseBugs evaluation drops the GNN component entirely.
threats_to_datum: Likely LLM memorization of BigVul is only partly mitigated via the temporally-filtered PreciseBugs set; BigVul itself has known label noise/selection bias from bug-fix-commit mining; the GNN was tuned specifically for BigVul's CFGs so the PreciseBugs generalization test omits it (Section 6).

title: LProtector: An LLM-driven Vulnerability Detection System
venue: arXiv (preprint; stated to appear in IEEE conference proceedings, specific venue unconfirmed)

key_numbers.metric: F1 (LProtector vs baselines)
ablation F1 (RAG+CoT vs No RAG)
ablation F1 (No RAG & No CoT)

structure_gain: Removing RAG context (holding GPT-4o and CoT fixed) drops F1 from 33.49% to 23.92%, a 9.57pp loss (Table III).
confound_note: Table III ablation varies retrieval context and CoT prompting independently while holding the GPT-4o model fixed -- a genuine representation-only ablation for the RAG factor; Table II comparison to VulDeePecker/Reveal changes model and method entirely.
threats_to_datum: 5-page short preprint; single-run reported numbers with no confidence intervals or variance; retrieval corpus drawn from the same Big-Vul dataset used for evaluation, raising potential train/retrieval-test leakage concerns.

title: Context-Enhanced Vulnerability Detection Based on Large Language Model

key_numbers.metric: F1, DeepSeek-R1+CoT: API-abstraction level A3 vs w/o-API context
F1 vs best context-sampling baseline (API-guided sampling)
CodeLLaMA+BP F1 vs best baseline (hierarchy sampling, HS-C)

structure_gain: A3 API-context vs w/o-API: F1 69.09% vs 60.89% (+8.20pp), same model (Table 4).
confound_note: The primary ablation (w/o-API vs A1-A4) holds model and code content fixed and varies only context abstraction level -- a clean representation-only comparison; the baseline comparison against All-Callees/Random/Hierarchy sampling additionally varies prompting strategy across models, so representation is not perfectly isolated there.
threats_to_datum: Static alias-analysis imprecision degrades the most abstract level (A4); DeepSeek-V3 shows high run-to-run performance volatility; evaluation limited to 623 historical CVE samples with no cross-project or production validation (Sections 5.1.3, 5.3.1, 6.2).

title: Tracing Errors, Constructing Fixes: Repository-Level Memory Error Repair via Typestate-Guided Context Retrieval
datasets: custom benchmark (14 real-world projects, 49 memory errors)

key_numbers.metric: correct patches, full LTFix vs. LTFix-NT (no context trace) ablation
total errors fixed, full LTFix vs. LTFix-F (file-level context) ablation
repair success rate (custom benchmark / SAVER dataset)

structure_gain: Full LTFix (typestate-guided context trace) vs. LTFix-NT (error-propagation path only, no context trace), same LLM (Claude 3.5 Sonnet): 22 vs. 15 correct patches (+47%), 37 vs. 22 total errors fixed (+68%), 1 vs. 4 new errors introduced (Section 5.7 ablation, RQ3).
confound_note: The LTFix-F / LTFix-M / LTFix-NT / full ablation fixes the LLM and prompting strategy, varying only the amount/structure of retrieved context (implicated files -> backtrace functions -> propagation path without trace -> full typestate-guided context trace), isolating the context-representation effect.
threats_to_datum: Evaluation relies on dynamic analysis requiring proof-of-concept inputs, so errors not exercised by available PoCs are missed; multi-threaded programs are explicitly excluded; LLM output validity is determined by a majority-of-5-runs threshold (4/5), introducing residual non-determinism.

title: Retrieval-Augmented Few-Shot Prompting Versus Fine-Tuning for Code Vulnerability Detection
venue: FLLM2025 (3rd International Conference on Foundation and Large Language Models)
datasets: Draper VDISC-derived labeled snippets (Russell et al. 2018), 4 CWE categories: CWE-119/120/469/476

key_numbers.metric: F1 / partial-match, 20-shot retrieval-augmented
F1 / partial-match, zero-shot baseline
fine-tuned comparators
key_numbers.value: Fine-tuned Gemini-1.5-Flash 59.31% F1 vs Fine-tuned CodeBERT 91.22% F1

structure_gain: Retrieval-augmented 20-shot prompting raises F1 from 36.35% (zero-shot) to 74.05%, same Gemini-1.5-Flash model (Table I) -- retrieval of semantically similar labeled examples is the sole varied factor across the few-shot arms.
confound_note: Few-shot arms (random vs retrieval-augmented vs retrieval-based labeling) hold the base model fixed and vary only the example-selection mechanism -- a clean representation-only ablation; the separate fine-tuned CodeBERT/Gemini comparisons change both model and training paradigm.
threats_to_datum: Dataset restricted to 4 CWE categories from a single source (Russell et al. 2018), limiting generalizability; only one base LLM (Gemini-1.5-Flash) tested across the prompting arms.

title: VulnAgent-R2: Evidence-Calibrated Multi-Agent Auditing for Repository-Level Vulnerability Detection

key_numbers.metric: F1/AUROC (Devign)
F1/AUROC (PrimeVul)
F1 ablation on PrimeVul, full vs. w/o graph optimizer

structure_gain: Full VulnAgent-R2 (bounded graph-context optimizer) vs. w/o graph optimizer, same base LLM (Qwen2.5-Coder-32B), on PrimeVul: F1 0.385 vs. 0.337 (Table 10); w/o CER 0.359, w/o Sceptic 0.352, w/o VPS 0.346 -- each context/verification component contributes measurably.
confound_note: Table 10 removes one architectural component (graph optimizer / counterfactual evidence reweighting / Sceptic / verification-plan synthesis) at a time while holding the base LLM and remaining pipeline fixed, isolating each context/verification mechanism's marginal contribution to F1.
threats_to_datum: Authors caution PrimeVul F1 remains modest (0.385) and describe the system as 'a prioritization aid rather than a replacement for manual review'; some ablation deltas are small relative to likely LLM sampling variance, and build-environment/runtime-assumption failures account for 23.8% of errors.

title: VulTriage: Triple-Path Context Augmentation for LLM-Based Vulnerability Detection

key_numbers.metric: P-C (Pair-wise Correct) vs VulTrial
F1 vs ConColl
Control Path ablation (P-C / Error)

structure_gain: Removing the structural Control Path (AST/CFG/DFG-derived) drops P-C from 55 to 42 (-23.6% relative) and raises errors from 76 to 89, same GPT-4o backend and test subset (Table 2).
confound_note: Table 2 ablation isolates each of the three context paths (Control/Knowledge/Semantic) with GPT-4o held fixed -- a clean representation-only comparison; Table 1's comparison to VulTrial/ConColl and other baselines confounds representation with differing system architectures.
threats_to_datum: Fixed three-path design with no adaptive per-language/per-vulnerability-type selection; no project-specific coding rules or historical patches incorporated; Kotlin evaluation is small (118 functions, 10-round random split) and scope is function-level only.

title: Neuro-Symbolic Reasoning for Vulnerability Detection
datasets: Merged PrimeVul + ReposVul + R2Vul, 801 samples across 5 CWE classes

key_numbers.metric: CWE-415 F1 gain (Claude Code, LeanGuard vs Pure LLM)
CWE-416 F1 gain (Codex, LeanGuard vs Pure LLM)
CWE-416 / CWE-415 F1 vs Pure LLM (same DeepSeek-V4-Pro)

structure_gain: LeanGuard (AST-extraction + Lean 4 verification) vs Pure LLM, identical DeepSeek-V4-Pro backend and temperature=0: F1 +0.135 (CWE-416) and +0.191 (CWE-415) (Table IV) -- a clean same-model comparison isolating the neurosymbolic pipeline's contribution.
confound_note: The Pure-LLM-vs-LeanGuard comparison (Table IV) holds the LLM backend fixed, cleanly isolating the pipeline's effect; but the internal 'w/o AST' ablation (RQ2) is confounded because removing AST extraction also changes the LLM's task from filtering candidates to directly identifying guards/dereferences (Section V-D).
threats_to_datum: Each CWE class requires hand-built extraction rules, property templates, and auto-pairing logic; authors explicitly disclaim generalization to unseen CWE classes; function-level only with no whole-program reasoning; authors describe it as an exploratory prototype, not a deployable tool.
